overall.summary: Repair required. Fendi and the two-look structure remain legible, but product fidelity, outfit continuity and moving composites still fail. S12-WORDMARK-SCALE is RESOLVED in the supplied samples: lettering is no longer conspicuously oversized, although typography remains defective. S10 corridor visibility is repaired; cadence remains open. S07-CUT-TIMING is UNCERTAIN, not proven resolved: no sample covers its prior disputed boundary interval. The old centered-white S11 mark and navy shoulder blocking are removed, but their broader branding/construction defects persist in new forms.

shots.expected: S01: Real Fendi performance in the French Black Denim trucker jacket, medium eye-level framing with a subtle push, establishing the cold charcoal fitting room with one reflective mirror panel. Original closet must be eliminated.
observations: Performance occurs and identity remains visually credible: the cap, glasses, beard and facial proportions remain consistent through S01 frames at draft 0:00.167, 0:01.833 and 0:03.833.

The jacket is worn continuously over a black tee. Torso and sleeve coverage survive the arms-out and crossing gestures at S01 0:00.167, 0:00.500 and 0:00.833; no substantial garment disappearance or additional limb is evident in those samples.

Product truth fails: S01 0:01.167, 0:02.833 and 0:03.167 show a heavily washed silver-gray jacket with exaggerated pale seam outlines, rather than the reference's restrained black denim. A red tab beside the wearer-left chest pocket is also visible and is absent from the supplied reference; its lettering is unreadable.

The transformed charcoal room, screen-left wall illumination and dark falloff are present at S01 0:00.167 and 0:03.833. However, the central panel reads as a dark recess rather than a mirror multiplying the highlight.

Closet elimination is incomplete: a rounded door-hardware fragment protrudes beyond the screen-right waist in S01 0:00.833. Soft gray contamination also outlines the cap and shoulders at S01 0:02.833 and 0:03.167.

The medium, approximately eye-level presentation establishes the performer as requested at S01 0:00.167–0:03.833. The exact 2% push and downbeat landing cannot be certified from these separated silent samples.
shots.observed: The intended performance setup occurs, with credible Fendi identity and continuous on-body coverage, but the jacket's material/detail mismatch, residual source hardware and matte fringe prevent conformance. Evidence: S01 frames at draft 0:00.833, 0:01.167, 0:02.833 and 0:03.167.
shots.recommended_action: Correct Look 2 against the product reference, then propagate the same construction across S01/S03/S04. Remove retained door hardware and edge contamination, repair the pre-hook mirror response, and verify native-frame synchronization without changing the performance.

shots.expected: S02: One-bar generated insert showing product-true jacket hardware, with a slow push, cold hard lighting and black falloff; no synthetic performance.
observations: The fashion insert occurs: S02 0:04.000, 0:04.833 and 0:05.833 show a cropped neck, black tee, collar, placket and chest pockets. No face or separately performing figure appears in these samples.
The crop enlarges subtly and remains compositionally stable between S02 0:04.000 and 0:05.833. No conspicuous texture reset or flicker is demonstrated by the supplied insert samples.

The intended hardware-commercial purpose fails: buttons remain soft, flat gray shapes, while seam edges look heavily outlined. This is visible throughout S02 0:04.000, 0:05.000 and 0:05.833; the crop does not resolve convincing metal relief or reference-level denim detail.

Dark, cool tonality broadly connects the insert to the performance world at S02 0:04.000 and 0:05.833. The tight torso crop does not expose enough environment to verify the room or a distinct cold rim.
The cutaway is visibly present between S01 0:03.833 and S03 0:06.042, but those samples cannot establish its exact beat landing.
shots.observed: A stable, slowly enlarging jacket close-up replaces performance, but it magnifies soft generated garment details instead of delivering the requested product-true hardware macro. Evidence: S02 frames at draft 0:04.000, 0:05.000 and 0:05.833.
shots.recommended_action: Rebuild the insert from reference-accurate jacket hardware and denim detail. Preserve the specified duration, restrained push and cold lighting; do not enlarge another unresolved performance-generation crop.

shots.expected: S03: Real rapid-fire performance in the same French Black Denim trucker jacket, medium locked framing in the pre-hook fitting room, preserving the pointing and raised-arm gestures around song 54–55 seconds.
observations: The intended gesture passage occurs: S03 0:07.042 and 0:07.375, corresponding to song 54.255 and 54.588 seconds, show the raised screen-left forearm and palm gesture. Cap, glasses, beard and facial appearance remain credible at S03 0:06.042, 0:08.708 and 0:11.708.

The jacket remains on the torso and both arms through the raised-arm passage and subsequent hand-over-sleeve movement at S03 0:07.042, 0:08.375 and 0:08.708. No broad body or garment dropout is visible in those samples.

The wardrobe changes across the cutaway: S01 0:03.833 has a lighter, narrower-sleeved jacket with a red chest tab; S03 0:06.042 and 0:06.708 return with darker material, fuller sleeves, different pocket detailing and shorter-looking cuff placement. This is not one stable jacket construction.
S03 is darker than S01, but the garment still has shiny, strongly outlined surfaces and soft hardware rather than the reference's restrained denim finish. See S03 0:06.708, 0:09.042 and 0:11.042.

Source contamination remains visible over time: rounded door hardware appears beside the screen-right cuff/hip at S03 0:06.042 and 0:11.708; irregular pale material appears outside the screen-right upper sleeve at 0:10.708 and forms a conspicuous vertical patch beside the sleeve at 0:11.375.

The medium framing and replacement-room layout remain steady at S03 0:06.042, 0:09.042 and 0:11.708, but the central panel still does not visibly multiply the key highlight. A soft cap/shoulder fringe remains against the sharp room plate.
S03 0:11.708 remains S03 content and S04 0:11.958 is already the tighter shot. This brackets the transition but does not resolve the previous approximately one-frame label-offset finding.
shots.observed: The requested real-performance gesture passage is visible with intact clothing coverage, but garment construction resets after S02 and source-background fragments remain beside the moving silhouette. Evidence: S03 frames at draft 0:06.042, 0:07.042, 0:10.708, 0:11.375 and 0:11.708.
shots.recommended_action: Repair the moving matte and retained source objects, including the screen-right sleeve/flank gaps. Reconcile garment construction with the corrected S01/S04 jacket, retain the original gestures, and inspect the S03/S04 transition at native frame rate.

shots.expected: S04: A tighter, approximately 1.25× crop of the real master performance, retaining the same Look 2 jacket and pre-hook room to escalate into the drop.
observations: The tighter shot occurs: S04 0:11.958 enlarges both performer and room relative to S03 0:11.708. S04 0:12.625 and 0:13.292 sustain the tighter eye-level presentation, approximately fulfilling the framing escalation.

Identity remains credible through the head turns at S04 0:12.625, 0:13.292 and 0:14.625. The jacket remains worn over the black tee, including the crossed-forearm occlusion at S04 0:13.625; no major anatomical or garment-coverage collapse is evident.

This is not merely a crop of the preceding garment state: S03 0:11.708 has subdued dark hardware and different pocket/cuff detailing; S04 0:11.958 and 0:12.292 introduce conspicuously bright buttons and revised jacket detailing.

Product truth remains unsuccessful at S04 0:12.292, 0:12.958 and 0:14.625: bright blank-looking hardware, strongly outlined construction and smooth shiny surfaces do not reproduce the supplied black-denim reference. No large external wordmark is required by that reference; button-level branding cannot be resolved here.
The charcoal replacement room remains visible at S04 0:11.958–0:14.625, but its central panel still reads as a dark architectural surface, not the specified highlight-multiplying mirror.

Composite defects remain: S04 0:12.625 exposes a pale sliver between the screen-right jacket hem and arm, and 0:13.625 shows a pale patch beyond the sleeve below the crossing forearm. Soft silhouette contamination is also visible around the cap/shoulder boundary at 0:12.625 and along the moving screen-right arm at 0:14.292.

Scoped re-review summary: no in-scope legacy visual defect is verified RESOLVED. The wardrobe, mirror and matte findings remain visible in S01 0:03.167, S02 0:05.000, S03 0:11.375 and S04 0:13.625. SEQ-CUT-BOUNDARY-OFFSET remains UNCERTAIN, not cleared, because S03 0:11.708 and S04 0:11.958 are not adjacent boundary frames. Both synchronization gates remain unverified. Supplied evidence ends at S04 0:14.625; S05–S12 findings are unreviewed, not resolved.
shots.observed: The intended punch-in and performance escalation occur, but the cut also changes garment details, while product-truth and compositing failures remain visible in the enlarged view. Evidence: S03 0:11.708 compared with S04 frames at draft 0:11.958, 0:12.292, 0:12.625 and 0:13.625.
shots.recommended_action: Preserve the requested punch-in, but derive it from the same corrected garment construction as S03. Repair sleeve-gap contamination and matte fringes, restore the mirror's specified response, and verify the cut and performance timing using native-frame audiovisual evidence.

shots.expected: A half-bar diamond-refraction insert with a slow push, cold highlights and black falloff, whitening the frame immediately before the hook.
observations: Frames S05 @ 0:14.833, 0:15.167 and 0:15.500 show a stable faceted diamond enlarging gradually against black, with cold spectral streaks. The requested insert occurs; no performer or wardrobe is required or visible.

Frame S05 @ 0:15.667 shows a substantial flash ramp, but the diamond remains visible against gray. The next supplied frame, S06 @ 0:15.875, already shows normally exposed performance. The intervening whiteout peak and flash handoff are UNCERTAIN, confidence 0.30; these samples do not establish a missing flash.
The gemstone and surrounding streaks remain structurally consistent from S05 @ 0:14.833 through 0:15.500. No conspicuous morphing or unintended subject appears in those samples.
shots.observed: The intended diamond insert and flash buildup occur. Full-frame whiteout and its precise musical landing cannot be verified from the supplied boundary samples.
shots.recommended_action: Inspect the native frames across the S05/S06 boundary with audio. Verify the whiteout peak and hook landing before changing the otherwise conforming diamond insert.

shots.expected: Fendi's real medium, eye-level performance introduces the reference Saint Laurent mastic/navy track jacket in the harder, multi-mirror ice room, preserving identity, pose and scale.
observations: Frames S06 @ 0:15.875, 0:16.542 and 0:20.542 retain a credible Fendi likeness: cap, glasses, beard and recognizable performance gestures. The jacket follows his torso and arms; black trousers cover the lower body. No wholesale garment disappearance or floating jacket is visible in these samples. Exact preservation of the native performance cannot be certified from the contact sheet alone.

Frames S06 @ 0:17.208, 0:18.542 and 0:20.542 show a jacket open almost to the waist, a long exposed tie, projecting striped shirt cuffs and an untucked shirt hem beneath a short jacket. This does not reproduce the reference's largely closed body and restrained shirt-and-tie exposure at the neck.

At S06 @ 0:15.875 and 0:18.542, the outstretched sleeves do not show the reference navy inner-sleeve runs. Narrow chest bands and a dark-lined raised collar are present, but those improvements do not establish product truth.

At S06 @ 0:15.875, a recognizable closet-side clothing pile/storage structure survives behind the screen-right arm and hip. At 0:18.542, an opaque pale wedge remains beneath the screen-left forearm. The transformed room has not completely replaced the source background.

Frames S06 @ 0:16.875 and 0:18.875 show broad pale silhouette echoes beside the screen-right sleeve; 0:20.542 shows an irregular, bitten outer sleeve edge. These change with movement rather than behaving like a controlled cold rim.

The wearer-left gold wordmark is visible at S06 @ 0:16.875, 0:17.542 and 0:20.542, but its glyph shapes change and its lettering is heavier than the supplied reference. Placement is improved; typography and temporal stability remain failed.

Frames S06 @ 0:18.208 and 0:21.542 show stable multiple reflective panels, hard highlights and wall/floor glints. The eye-level, upper-leg-inclusive performance framing approximately matches the requested medium shot. The drop's performance-and-room change is visible, but the product and composite failures prevent conformance.
shots.observed: Fendi performs wearing a beige/navy jacket and the expanded outfit in the intended mirror room. However, the jacket is not product-correct, branding remains unstable, recognizable source-background material survives, and moving matte contamination is conspicuous.
shots.recommended_action: Remove retained source-background components and repair moving matte edges. Correct the jacket against both product references, then propagate that approved construction and tracked reference wordmark without changing Fendi's performance.

shots.expected: A one-bar luxury/night-city cutaway answering 'ice on', with a slow push, cold illumination, black falloff and no synthetic performer.
observations: Frames S07 @ 0:21.708, 0:22.542 and 0:23.542 show a rain-speckled vehicle-window view of blue-white city lights and wet-road reflections. The requested cold night-city motif occurs; no performer or garment is introduced.

Across S07 @ 0:21.708–0:23.542, the window, droplets and light pattern undergo a gradual lateral/scale move without conspicuous geometry morphing. This is consistent with the requested slow-push cutaway rather than a new performance shot.

The previous early-city label discrepancy is not reproduced in the supplied pair: S06 @ 0:21.542 is still performance and S07 @ 0:21.708 is city, bracketing the declared 0:21.639 boundary. shots.recommended_action: Retain the city visual. Verify the actual incoming and outgoing cut frames on the native presentation-time grid; do not shift the edit based on these sparse samples.

observations: Frames S08 @ 0:23.750, 0:24.417, 0:27.417 and 0:29.417 retain a credible cap/glasses/beard identity through head turns and crossed-arm movement. Clothing remains attached to the torso and sleeves, and arm-over-body occlusion broadly follows the performance. Frames S08 @ 0:23.750 and 0:24.750 show pale cream sleeves against a distinctly tan body, a pale inner stand collar, dark zipper/pocket outlines and an opening exposing the tie below the chest stripe. At 0:28.417, the visible forearm surfaces still lack the reference inner-sleeve navy runs. This is not the supplied track-jacket construction.

Comparing S06 @ 0:21.542 with S08 @ 0:23.750 and 0:24.083, the outfit resets across the city insert: the short, dark-lined-collar jacket with exposed striped cuffs and shirt hem becomes a longer two-tone jacket with a pale collar interior, dark zipper and different cuff/hem treatment. No wardrobe change is specified.

The lower waistband is defined at S08 @ 0:24.750, loses that construction at 0:26.083 and 0:26.750, returns at 0:27.417, and is again poorly defined at 0:29.083. The lower front remains visible during these changes; this is not explained solely by crossed-arm occlusion.

At S08 @ 0:23.750, a dark, pale-edged non-room fragment remains behind the screen-right hip, between torso and arm. Its precise source object is uncertain, but its failure to belong to the mirror plate is visible.

Frames S08 @ 0:24.083 and 0:26.417 show broad pale contamination above and beside the shoulders; 0:25.417 shows an irregular screen-left sleeve boundary. The foreground remains visibly softer and more cut out than the sharp mirror plate.

The gold wearer-left wordmark remains incorrectly drawn and changes across S08 @ 0:24.083, 0:24.417 and 0:27.417. Its lettering is more prominent and heavier than the delicate reference mark; the scale assessment is moderate confidence, while the typography failure is clear.

The room and approximate framing remain consistent between S08 @ 0:23.750, 0:26.083 and 0:29.417: multiple reflective panels, cold glints, deep black and a locked eye-level performance view. The second-repeat performance occurs, but product continuity and integration fail.

Historical tracking: PERF-CLOSET-LEAKAGE remains PRESENT at S08 @ 0:23.750; that same physical return-frame remnant is reported once below as HOOK-SOURCE-LEAK. REVIEW-SYNC-UNVERIFIED remains an open uncertainty and is represented once by SEQ-FRAME-SYNC-UNVERIFIED.

Re-review summary, S05–S08 only: REPAIR_REQUIRED. No complete historical defect ID is certified RESOLVED by this subset. The old pointed outer collar and shoulder-tab appearance is absent in S08 @ 0:23.750 and 0:27.417, but the jacket still fails construction and continuity. Pre-hook and S09–S12-specific findings, including the cited late-shot components of HOOK-LOOK1-GARMENT-TRUTH and HOOK-WORDMARK-DRIFT, are not reviewed or cleared.

shots.recommended_action: Restore the reference jacket's sleeve, collar, closure, pocket and hem construction; use one approved garment state across S06 and S08. Stabilize its seams and wordmark through arm crossings, and remove the return-frame source remnant and moving matte contamination.

shots.expected: Real crossed-arm performance in Look 1: Saint Laurent mastic/navy track jacket, medium eye-level locked framing, in the cold multi-mirror room. Preserve Fendi's identity, gestures and source timing.
observations: Shot purpose occurs: S09 @ 0:29.583–0:31.083 shows crossed arms, head turns and a forward dip; S09 @ 0:31.250–0:31.417 shows the arms beginning to uncross. Source-clock verification remains UNCERTAIN, low confidence: crossed arms at S09 @ 0:29.583–0:30.917 support the intended gesture, but do not validate the assembled 1.000-second asset trim. No audible or native-frame sync conclusion is possible.

Earlier-only legacy findings are NOT REVIEWABLE here, not resolved: SEQ-LOOK2-PRODUCT-TRUTH, SEQ-MIRROR-PROGRESSION-MISSING, LOOK2-PRODUCT-TRUTH, PREHOOK-MATTE-HALO, LOOK2-CUT-CONSTRUCTION-DRIFT, S02-HARDWARE-MACRO-TRUTH, PREHOOK-CLOSET-MATTE-LEAK, PERF-MATTE-COVERAGE, LOOK1-CONSTRUCTION-MISMATCH, LOOK1-WORDMARK-TRUTH, S06-S08-GARMENT-RESET, PERF-CLOSET-LEAKAGE, HOOK-SOURCE-LEAK and S07-CUT-TIMING. shots.recommended_action: Correct the reference-specific cuff, hem and fabric construction without replacing the performance. Propagate one approved outfit and tracked wordmark across the hook, clean the silhouette fringe, and verify the S09 asset-to-master mapping before any retiming.

The supplied labels bracket the cuts consistently: S09 @ 0:31.417 precedes the declared 0:31.475 boundary, S10 @ 0:31.542 follows it; S10 @ 0:33.375 precedes 0:33.443 and S11 @ 0:33.583 follows it. These gaps cannot establish or exclude a one-frame boundary offset.

shots.recommended_action: No visual regeneration is indicated. Verify native-frame cut placement and strobe cadence against the song clock; the visual PASS does not certify audio synchronization.

However, the tall flared collar presents a mastic inner face instead of the reference's navy lining, and the exposed sleeve surfaces remain plain where the reference requires inner-sleeve navy panels. The spread-arm view at 0:34.250 is particularly useful evidence.

New foreground erosion is visible at S11 @ 0:34.583: the screen-right collar/shoulder and outer sleeve become a jagged, stepped silhouette. Compare the more intact outline at 0:34.250 and 0:35.250. This is not believable rim lighting or garment folding.

The first supplied S11 frame is 0:33.583, after the declared 0:33.443 entrance. The requested glitch transition and one-frame lip synchronization remain UNCERTAIN; their absence cannot be inferred from this sampling.

shots.recommended_action: Repair foreground retention and remove attached background remnants first. Then correct the collar lining and inner-sleeve panels, replace the stacked pseudo-text with the reference wordmark, and match construction to the adjoining hook assets.
